notes: The clearest policy in this union. The 2026 packet's guideline page prints 'November 1, 2026 for 2026 projects and May 1, 2027 ... for the rest of 2027', which conflicts with the web page (1 November for the following year); treat 1 November 2026 as the deadline for 2027 series and confirm with the department. The department director changed in September 2026 (use the role, not a name). Church volunteer forms printed before June 2026 are void.

notes: The guidelines point to scc.adventist.org/departments-ministries/evangelism, but that address now redirects to an old 2020 story; the guideline, application and SOP files were found through the site's own media library (links above). No deadline is published. Note the trade-off: a church that applies to the Pacific Union Endowment Fund cannot receive the SCC fund in the same year. SCC works through five regions (Asian-Pacific, Greater Los Angeles, Hispanic, Los Angeles Metropolitan, West); the region director must sign, and regions may have their own funds. No honorarium rule was found. Union money: a church may also apply to the Pacific Union Evangelism Endowment Fund for creative or innovative projects, through the conference president’s office (2026 conference deadline 24 Sep; 2027 conference deadlines 28 Jan and 7 Oct). The union says about $1M a year is released from this fund.

notes: The mission's website (gmmsda.org) publishes no evangelism funding policy, honorarium rule or child-protection policy; its Ministerial entry on the departments page is a placeholder. It is an attached field of the North American Division, so the Pacific Union Evangelism Endowment Fund does not apply. The childProtection sources are the NAD-wide Adventist Screening Verification rule (Sterling Volunteers, every three years), not a mission-specific policy. Three of the five areas (Federated States of Micronesia, Palau, Marshall Islands) are independent countries, so US state law does not apply there.
